### **You**

# NASA Eyes on the Solar System 中文本地化项目

你现在担任本项目的全栈开发工程师。

## 一、项目目标

原始网站：

https://eyes.nasa.gov/apps/solar-system/#/home

开发一个可以在浏览器中访问的、面向中文用户的非官方 NASA 太阳系 3D 探索网站。

核心目标：

1. 最大限度保留 NASA 原版 3D 模拟器的功能。
2. 将用户能够操作和阅读的界面尽可能翻译成简体中文。
3. 尽可能保留原始太阳系模型、航天器轨迹、时间轴和视角控制。
4. 提供中文天体名称、航天任务介绍和操作说明。
5. 后续可以部署到 GitHub Pages 或其他静态网站托管平台。
6. 保持页面简洁、美观，适合桌面浏览器。

**不要从零重新开发行星动力学或 3D 引擎，除非通过技术验证确认确有必要，并获得我的同意。**

## 二、第一阶段：技术可行性调查

在编写功能代码之前，先使用实际网页、浏览器开发者工具及必要的自动化浏览器工具，检查：

- NASA 网站的页面加载方式和可访问性。
- 3D 场景的实际渲染机制。
- 菜单、按钮、文字的具体来源。
- 哪些文字属于 HTML DOM，哪些属于 Canvas、WebGL 或其他渲染层。
- 网站是否具有现成的国际化或多语言机制。
- 官方 iframe 嵌入方式是否正常。
- 是否可以通过 URL 参数控制视图、天体和时间。
- 普通独立网站能否访问嵌入页面的内部内容。

所有判断必须基于实际验证。

不要猜测任何 DOM 选择器、资源路径、接口名称、配置字段或源码结构。

## 三、第二阶段：制定汉化方案

分别评估：

方案 A：Chrome/Edge 浏览器扩展，通过页面注入翻译原始 NASA 网站。

方案 B：独立中文网站，嵌入 NASA 官方 3D 模拟器，并提供中文界面和说明。

方案 C：在获得相应使用权限及技术依据后，独立实现必要的中文交互层。

分析各方案能够覆盖的文字、不能覆盖的功能、维护成本和使用限制。

优先采用能够保留原始功能、修改量较小、便于持续维护的方案。

## 四、第三阶段：实现最小可用版本

如果独立网站方案验证可行，先实现：

1. 首页和中文导航。
2. NASA 官方 3D 太阳系嵌入区域。
3. 太阳、八大行星及主要天体的中文名称。
4. 常用交互操作的中文说明。
5. 常见航天器和任务的中文介绍入口。
6. 中文与英文术语对照。
7. 可访问原始 NASA 网站的入口。
8. 清楚标注哪些内容仍保留英文。

如果官方支持的深层链接已通过实际测试，可增加中文快捷导航，直接跳转指定天体或任务。

不要使用未经验证的内部 API。

## 五、中文翻译质量

建立可维护的中文术语表。

翻译要求：

- 天文学专有名词准确。
- 行星、卫星及航天器名称采用规范中文译名。
- 必要时保留英文原文。
- 数字、日期、距离和单位不能因翻译发生变化。
- 没有可靠译名的项目保持原文并标记。

翻译文本与页面逻辑分离，便于维护。

## 六、技术与合规要求

- 优先考虑无需后端的静态网站。
- 不得通过不安全方式绕过浏览器同源策略。
- 不得擅自声称 NASA 软件本体已经开源。
- 不得擅自复制或重新发布未经确认许可的软件资源。
- 网站明显标注“非官方中文项目”。
- 保留原始 NASA 来源和必要的素材署名。
- 遵守 NASA/JPL 的素材使用和品牌规范。

## 七、测试验收

至少验证：

- 页面正常打开，3D 场景成功加载。
- 鼠标旋转、缩放等原有功能正常。
- 中文导航可以正常使用。
- 已实现的天体及航天器入口可以到达预期页面。
- 原始网站的功能没有因中文界面而失效。
- 不存在明显遮挡、错位或无法退出的界面。
- Chrome 与 Edge 桌面浏览器正常使用。
- 对无法实现的汉化范围给出准确说明。

## 八、工作流程

首先完成技术调查，输出：

1. 实际网站结构与技术证据。
2. 三种汉化方案的可行性比较。
3. 建议实现方案与原因。
4. 中文界面覆盖范围。
5. 无法汉化的部分及原因。
6. 最小可用版本的开发计划。

技术调查完成后，如果没有发现重大阻碍，可继续实现最小可用版本并进行本地验证。

若发现与核心需求冲突的技术限制，必须先报告，不得擅自用功能明显缩水的页面代替原有目标。

#### Thinking

**MAJOR FINDING**: All celestial body and spacecraft labels in the 3D scene are **DOM elements** — `<div class="pioneer-label-div ..."><span class="icon ..."></span><span class="text ">Sun</span></div>`, positioned via CSS `translate: Xpx Ypx`.

This means:
1. Planet/spacecraft names in the 3D view are translatable via DOM text replacement (MutationObserver) — no need to touch WebGL.
2. Each label has a semantic class name (`earth`, `mars`, `sc_new_horizons`) — a stable key for a translation table!

This dramatically changes the feasibility analysis: a Chrome extension (方案 A) could translate nearly everything, AND an iframe approach cannot (cross-origin DOM access blocked).

#### Tool: Write

**Input:**

```json
{
  "content": "// Dependency-free CDP driver for headless Chrome (Node >= 21, global WebSocket).\n// Usage:\n//   node cdp.mjs probe <exprFile> [url]     evaluate expression, print JSON result\n//   node cdp.mjs shot  <outPng> [url]       full screenshot\n// Chrome must already be listening: see chrome-start.mjs\nconst [mode, arg, urlArg] = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst PORT = process.env.CDP_PORT || '9333';\nconst DEFAULT_URL = 'https://eyes.nasa.gov/apps/solar-system/#/home';\n\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n\nasync function targetWs() {\n  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`);\n      const list = await res.json();\n      const page = list.find((t) => t.type === 'page');\n      if (page) return page.webSocketDebuggerUrl;\n    } catch {}\n    await sleep(500);\n  }\n  throw new Error('no CDP page target');\n}\n\nclass Cdp {\n  constructor(ws) {\n    this.ws = ws;\n    this.id = 0;\n    this.pending = new Map();\n    ws.onmessage = (ev) => {\n      const msg = JSON.parse(ev.data);\n      if (msg.id && this.pending.has(msg.id)) {\n        const { resolve, reject } = this.pending.get(msg.id);\n        this.pending.delete(msg.id);\n        msg.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result);\n      }\n    };\n  }\n  send(method, params = {}) {\n    const id = ++this.id;\n    this.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));\n    return new Promise((resolve, reject) =>\n      this.pending.set(id, { resolve, reject }),\n    );\n  }\n  async evaluate(expression) {\n    const r = await this.send('Runtime.evaluate', {\n      expression,\n      returnByValue: true,\n      awaitPromise: true,\n    });\n    if (r.exceptionDetails)\n      throw new Error('page exception: ' + JSON.stringify(r.exceptionDetails).slice(0, 800));\n    return r.result.value;\n  }\n}\n\nconst wrap = (expr) =>\n  `(async () => { const fn = (${expr}); return await fn(); })()`;\n\nasync function main() {\n  const ws = new WebSocket(await targetWs());\n  await new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));\n  ws.onerror = (e) => console.error('ws error', e.message?.value ?? '');\n  const cdp = new Cdp(ws);\n  await cdp.send('Runtime.enable');\n  await cdp.send('Page.enable');\n  await cdp.send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', {\n    width: 1600, height: 900, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false,\n  });\n\n  const url = urlArg || DEFAULT_URL;\n  await cdp.send('Page.navigate', { url });\n  // NASA Eyes streams assets for a while; poll until the scene reports ready.\n  await cdp.evaluate(\n    `(async () => {\n      for (let i = 0; i < 120; i++) {\n        const ls = document.getElementById('loading-screen');\n        const hidden = !ls || getComputedStyle(ls).display === 'none' || getComputedStyle(ls).opacity === '0';\n        if (hidden && document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div').length > 3) return 'ready';\n        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000));\n      }\n      return 'timeout';\n    })()`,\n  );\n\n  if (mode === 'probe') {\n    const { readFileSync } = await import('node:fs');\n    const expr = readFileSync(arg, 'utf8');\n    console.log(JSON.stringify(await cdp.evaluate(wrap(expr)), null, 2));\n  } else if (mode === 'shot') {\n    const r = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' });\n    const { writeFileSync } = await import('node:fs');\n    writeFileSync(arg, Buffer.from(r.data, 'base64'));\n    console.log('wrote ' + arg);\n  } else {\n    throw new Error('unknown mode ' + mode);\n  }\n  ws.close();\n}\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error('FAIL: ' + e.message);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/research/cdp.mjs"
}

{
  "content": "() => {\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  const visible = (el) => {\n    const cs = getComputedStyle(el);\n    if (cs.display === 'none' || cs.visibility === 'hidden' || cs.opacity === '0') return false;\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return r.width > 0 && r.height > 0;\n  };\n  // Collect every DOM node that carries user-visible text, with a stable-ish selector.\n  const path = (el) => {\n    const parts = [];\n    let n = el;\n    while (n && n !== document.body && parts.length < 5) {\n      let s = n.tagName.toLowerCase();\n      if (n.id) s = '#' + n.id;\n      else if (n.className && typeof n.className === 'string') {\n        const c = clean(n.className).split(' ').filter(Boolean).slice(0, 2).join('.');\n        if (c) s += '.' + c;\n      }\n      parts.unshift(s);\n      n = n.parentElement;\n    }\n    return parts.join(' > ');\n  };\n  const texts = [];\n  const seen = new Set();\n  document.querySelectorAll('#static-ui *, #dynamic-ui *, body > div *').forEach((el) => {\n    if (el.children.length) return;\n    const t = clean(el.textContent);\n    if (!t || t.length > 160) return;\n    if (!visible(el)) return;\n    const key = path(el) + '|' + t;\n    if (seen.has(key)) return;\n    seen.add(key);\n    texts.push({ text: t, where: path(el) });\n  });\n  return {\n    url: location.href,\n    pageTitle: document.title,\n    canvasCount: document.querySelectorAll('canvas').length,\n    labelDivs: document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div').length,\n    totalDomNodes: document.querySelectorAll('*').length,\n    visibleTextNodes: texts.length,\n    texts,\n  };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/research/probe_home_text.mjs"
}

Object.keys(window[r]).slice(0, 25) : String(window[r]).slice(0, 120); } catch (e) {}\n  }\n  // The menu list is our reliable, DOM-visible entity catalogue.\n  const menu = document.querySelector('.menu-container');\n  out.menuPresent = !!menu;\n  if (menu) {\n    const blocks = [...menu.querySelectorAll('.block')].map((b) => ({\n      title: clean(b.querySelector('.title')?.textContent),\n      items: [...b.querySelectorAll('li, .item, [class*=entity]')].map((li) => ({\n        txt: clean(li.textContent).slice(0, 80),\n        cls: clean(li.className),\n        id: li.getAttribute('id') || li.dataset?.id || null,\n      })).filter((x) => x.txt).slice(0, 60),\n    }));\n    out.blocks = blocks;\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n",

{
  "content": "() => {\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n  const map = { Sun: '太阳', Earth: '地球', Mars: '火星', Jupiter: '木星', Saturn: '土星', Venus: '金星', Mercury: '水星', Uranus: '天王星', Neptune: '海王星', Moon: '月球' };\n  const snap = () => [...document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div .text')].map((e) => clean(e.textContent));\n  const apply = () => {\n    document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div').forEach((d) => {\n      const t = d.querySelector('.text');\n      if (t && map[clean(t.textContent)]) t.textContent = map[clean(t.textContent)];\n    });\n  };\n  const out = { before: snap() };\n  // Count how often the app rewrites label text on its own.\n  let mutations = 0;\n  const touched = new Set();\n  const obs = new MutationObserver((recs) => {\n    recs.forEach((r) => {\n      mutations++;\n      const n = r.target.nodeType === 3 ? r.target.parentElement : r.target;\n      touched.add(clean(n?.textContent).slice(0, 30));\n    });\n  });\n  obs.observe(document.getElementById('main-viewport'), { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });\n  apply();\n  out.afterApply = snap();\n  await wait(6000);\n  out.after6s = snap();\n  out.mutationCountIn6s = mutations;\n  out.mutatedNodes = [...touched].slice(0, 25);\n  // Now test whether a camera move (wheel zoom) reverts them.\n  const vp = document.getElementById('main-viewport');\n  const r = vp.getBoundingClientRect();\n  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {\n    vp.dispatchEvent(new WheelEvent('wheel', { deltaY: -120, clientX: r.width / 2, clientY: r.height / 2, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }));\n    await wait(120);\n  }\n  await wait(3000);\n  out.afterZoom = snap();\n  out.stillChinese = out.afterZoom.filter((t) => /[一-龥]/.test(t)).length;\n  obs.disconnect();\n  return out;\n}\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/research/probe_label_persistence.mjs"
}

{
  "content": "() => {\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n  const harvest = () => {\n    const texts = new Set();\n    const attrs = new Set();\n    document.querySelectorAll('*').forEach((el) => {\n      if (el.children.length === 0) {\n        const t = clean(el.textContent);\n        if (t && t.length <= 120 && /[a-z]/i.test(t)) texts.add(t);\n      }\n      for (const a of ['aria-label', 'title', 'data-tippy-content', 'placeholder', 'alt']) {\n        const v = clean(el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute(a));\n        if (v && v.length <= 160) attrs.add(v);\n      }\n    });\n    return { texts, attrs };\n  };\n  const acc = { texts: new Set(), attrs: new Set() };\n  const merge = () => { const h = harvest(); h.texts.forEach((t) => acc.texts.add(t)); h.attrs.forEach((t) => acc.attrs.add(t)); };\n  merge();\n\n  // Enumerate the right-hand settings bar icons without guessing their class names.\n  const bars = [...document.querySelectorAll('[class*=settings], [class*=shortcut], nav, aside')]\n    .filter((e) => { const r = e.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 0 && r.right > innerWidth - 140 && r.height > 40; });\n  const icons = [...new Set(bars.flatMap((b) => [...b.querySelectorAll('[class*=icon]')]))];\n  const trail = icons.map((el, i) => ({ i, cls: clean(el.className), tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase() }));\n  for (let i = 0; i < icons.length; i++) {\n    try { icons[i].click(); } catch {}\n    await wait(1100);\n    merge();\n    try { icons[i].click(); } catch {}   // close again so panels don't stack\n    await wait(500);\n  }\n  merge();\n  return {\n    route: location.hash,\n    domNodes: document.querySelectorAll('*').length,\n    iconTrail: trail,\n    texts: [...acc.texts],\n    attrs: [...acc.attrs],\n  };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/research/probe_harvest.mjs"
}
```

Hmm, duplicating data files between site and extension is a maintenance smell. Better: keep the canonical data in `assets/data/` and have the extension reference the same files by copying at packaging time... For a static, no-build project, simplest is: put shared dictionaries in a top-level `shared/` dir and have both `extension/manifest.json` web_accessible... no, extensions read their own files.

Cleanest without a build step: keep dictionaries in `data/` at project root; the site loads them via fetch; the extension also loads them via `chrome.runtime.getURL('data/...')` if we include `data/` in the extension folder. To avoid duplication, make the extension folder's data a relative reference — not possible in extensions.

Pragmatic: put the dictionaries in `data/`, and provide a tiny `build-extension.mjs` that copies `data/` + `content.js` into `extension/`. Actually simpler and honest: the extension ships with its own `data/` copy generated by a 10-line script. That's a real, maintainable solution.

Even simpler: make the project root itself the extension directory? No, messy.

Decision: canonical dictionaries live in `data/`. A `pack-extension.mjs` copies `data/*.json` + `extension/*` into `dist/extension/`. Clean, no duplication in source.

{
  "content": "// Keeps data/names.zh.json honest: every key must exist in the entity export,\n// and the recorded English name must equal what the site actually renders\n// (verified: label text === displayName || iauName, 28/28 against the live DOM).\n//\n//   node tools/sync-glossary.mjs <entities.json> <names.zh.json> [--write]\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\n\nconst [entitiesPath, namesPath, writeFlag] = process.argv.slice(2);\nif (!entitiesPath || !namesPath) {\n  console.error('usage: node tools/sync-glossary.mjs <entities.json> <names.zh.json> [--write]');\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nconst entities = JSON.parse(readFileSync(entitiesPath, 'utf8'));\nconst byId = new Map(entities.map((e) => [e.id, e]));\nconst glossary = JSON.parse(readFileSync(namesPath, 'utf8'));\nconst label = (e) => e.displayName || e.iauName || null;\n\nconst dropped = [];\nconst fixed = [];\nconst next = {};\n\nfor (const [id, entry] of Object.entries(glossary.entities)) {\n  const real = byId.get(id);\n  if (!real || !entry.zh) {\n    dropped.push(id);\n    continue;\n  }\n  const en = label(real);\n  if (entry.en !== en) fixed.push(`${id}: \"${entry.en}\" -> \"${en}\"`);\n  next[id] = { ...entry, en, cat: real.category };\n}\n\nglossary.entities = next;\nglossary.meta.totalEntities = entities.length;\nglossary.meta.coveredEntities = Object.keys(next).length;\nglossary.meta.nameFormula = 'displayName || iauName（与站点渲染标签实测一致）';\n\nconsole.log(`covered ${Object.keys(next).length} of ${entities.length} entities`);\nif (dropped.length) console.log('dropped:\\n  ' + dropped.join('\\n  '));\nif (fixed.length) console.log('corrected:\\n  ' + fixed.join('\\n  '));\nif (writeFlag === '--write') {\n  writeFileSync(namesPath, JSON.stringify(glossary, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  console.log('written: ' + namesPath);\n}\n",

}

### sun | Sun
The Sun—the heart of our solar system—is a yellow dwarf star, a hot ball of glowing gases.

### mercury | Mercury
The smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun, Mercury is only slightly larger than Earth's Moon.

### venus | Venus
Similar in size and structure to Earth, Venus has been called Earth's twin. These are not identical twins, however – there are radical differences between the two worlds.

### earth | Earth
Earth—our home planet—is the only place we know of so far that’s inhabited by living things. It's also the only planet in our solar system with liquid water on the surface.

### mars | Mars
The fourth planet from the Sun, Mars is a dusty, cold, desert world with a very thin atmosphere.

### jupiter | Jupiter
Jupiter is the fifth planet from our Sun and is, by far, the largest planet in the solar system – more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

### saturn | Saturn
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second largest planet in our solar system. Adorned with thousands of beautiful ringlets, Saturn is unique among the planets. It is not the only planet to have rings—made of chunks of ice and rock—but none are as spectacular or as complicated as Saturn's. Like fellow gas giant Jupiter, Saturn is a massive ball made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

### uranus | Uranus
The seventh planet from the Sun with the third largest diameter in our solar system, Uranus is very cold and windy.

### neptune | Neptune
Dark, cold and whipped by supersonic winds, ice giant Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet in our solar system.

### 134340_pluto | Pluto
Pluto – which is smaller than Earth’s Moon – has a heart-shaped glacier that’s the size of Texas and Oklahoma. This fascinating dwarf planet has blue skies, spinning moons, mountains as high as the Rockies, and it snows – but the snow is red.

### 1_ceres | 1 Ceres
Dwarf planet Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter and the only dwarf planet located in the inner solar system.

### moon | Moon
Earth's Moon is the only place beyond Earth where humans have set foot.

### titan | Titan
Saturn’s largest moon Titan is an extraordinary and exceptional world.

### europa | Europa
Europa may be the most promising place in our solar system to find present-day environments suitable for some form of life beyond Earth.

### ganymede | Ganymede
Jupiter's moon Ganymede is the largest moon in our solar system and the only moon with its own magnetic field.

### io | Io
Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active world in the Solar System, with hundreds of volcanoes, some erupting lava fountains dozens of miles (or kilometers) high.

### callisto | Callisto
Callisto is Jupiter’s second largest moon and the third largest moon in our solar system.

### enceladus | Enceladus
One of Saturn's most surprising moons, Enceladus has altered views about where life might exist.

### triton | Triton
Triton is the largest of Neptune's [##moon_count##] moons. It is unusual because it is the only large moon in our solar system that orbits in the opposite direction of its planet's rotation―a retrograde orbit.

### charon | Charon
At half the size of Pluto, Charon is the largest of Pluto's moons and the largest known satellite relative to its parent body.

### 16_psyche | 16 Psyche
Psyche is one of the largest asteroids in the solar system, and is mostly made of metal.

### 101955_bennu | 101955 Bennu
An ancient relic of our solar system’s early days, Bennu has seen more than 4.5 billion years of history. Scientists think that within 10 million years of our solar system’s formation, Bennu’s present-day composition was already established.

### sc_voyager_1 | Voyager 1
No spacecraft has gone farther than NASA's Voyager 1. Launched in 1977 to fly by Jupiter and Saturn, Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to collect data.
### sc_voyager_2 | Voyager 2
NASA's Voyager 2 is the second spacecraft to enter interstellar space. On Dec. 10, 2018, the spacecraft joined its twin—Voyager 1—as the only human-made objects to enter the space between the stars.
### sc_pioneer_10 | Pioneer 10
Launched in 1972, Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to visit Jupiter. Its mission ended in 2003, but it is one of four spacecraft (including the two Voyagers and Pioneer 11) carrying a message from Earth beyond our solar system.
### sc_pioneer_11 | Pioneer 11
Launched in 1973, Pioneer 11 was the first spacecraft to fly past Saturn. Its mission ended in 1995, but it is one of four spacecraft (including the two Voyagers and Pioneer 10) carrying a message from Earth beyond our solar system.
### sc_new_horizons | New Horizons
New Horizons is a NASA mission to study the dwarf planet Pluto, its moons, and other objects in the Kuiper Belt, a region of the solar system that extends from about 30 AU, near the orbit of Neptune, to about 50 AU from the Sun.
### sc_cassini | Cassini
For more than a decade, NASA’s Cassini spacecraft shared the wonders of Saturn and its family of icy moons—taking us to astounding worlds where methane rivers run to a methane sea and where jets of ice and gas are blasting material into space from a liquid water ocean that might harbor the ingredients for life. Cassini revealed in great detail the true wonders of Saturn, a giant world ruled by raging storms and delicate harmonies of gravity.
### sc_juno | Juno
Juno is studying the interior and origins of giant planet Jupiter for the first time. It has been orbiting Jupiter since it arrived in 2016.
### sc_europa_clipper | Europa Clipper
Europa Clipper will search for signs of potential habitability on Jupiter's icy ocean moon Europa.
### sc_parker_solar_probe | Parker Solar Probe
NASA's Parker Solar Probe is on a mission to "touch the Sun." The spacecraft is flying closer to the Sun’s surface than any spacecraft before it. The mission will revolutionize our understanding of the Sun.
### sc_jwst | James Webb Space Telescope
The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is a large infrared telescope with an approximately 6.5 meter primary mirror.
### sc_hubble_space_telescope | Hubble Space Telescope
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope is the first astronomical observatory placed into orbit around Earth with the ability to record images in wavelengths of light spanning from ultraviolet to near-infrared.
### sc_roman_space_telescope | Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
Named after NASA’s first chief astronomer, the ‘mother of the Hubble Space Telescope,’ the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble's, potentially measuring light from a billion galaxies in its lifetime. The mission launched on August 30, 2026.
### sc_mars_2020 | Perseverance
The Perseverance rover is looking for signs of ancient life and is collecting rock and soil samples for a possible return to Earth by a subsequent Mars mission.
### sc_mars_science_laboratory | Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity)
Part of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory mission, Curiosity was the largest and most capable rover ever sent to Mars at the time of launch.
### sc_insight | InSight
NASA's InSight lander (Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport) is the first mission to study the deep interior of Mars.
### sc_phoenix | Phoenix
NASA's Phoenix mission landed farther north on Mars than any previous spacecraft to date. The lander verified the presence of water-ice on Mars by actually scooping it up and analyzing it.
### sc_iss | International Space Station (ISS)
The International Space Station (ISS) is a permanently crewed on-orbit laboratory that enables scientific research supporting innovation on Earth and future deep space exploration.
### sc_lucy | Lucy
The <a href='https://science.nasa.gov/mission/lucy/' target='_blank'>Lucy</a> spacecraft will explore a record-breaking number of asteroids, flying by two asteroids in the solar system’s main asteroid belt, and by eight Trojan asteroids that share an orbit around the Sun with Jupiter.
### sc_psyche | Psyche
The <a href='https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/missions/psyche' target='_blank'>Psyche</a> mission launched on October 13th, 2023, and will explore the origin of planetary cores by studying the metallic asteroid of the same name.
### sc_osiris_rex | OSIRIS-APEX (OSIRIS-REx)
NASA’s <a href='https://www.nasa.gov/osiris-rex' target='_blank'>OSIRIS-REx</a> was the first U.S. mission to deliver an asteroid sample to Earth on September 24th, 2023. The spacecraft, renamed OSIRIS-APEX after the delivery, is now headed to asteroid Apophis for a 2029 rendezvous.
### sc_dart | DART
<a href='https://dart.jhuapl.edu/' target='_blank'>DART</a>, or Double Asteroid Redirection Test, was the first attempt to change the course of an asteroid with a kinetic impact.
### sc_artemis_1 | Artemis I
Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test that was the first mission to use NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and the Orion spacecraft. It was followed by a crewed flight on Artemis II in April of 2026.
### sc_artemis_2 | Artemis II
Artemis II built on the success of the uncrewed Artemis I in 2022, and demonstrated a broad range of capabilities needed on deep space missions. The Artemis II test flight was NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft. The Artemis II crew traveled approximately 6,545 kilometers (4,067 miles) beyond the far side of the Moon on April 6th, 2026, setting a human spaceflight distance record. Artemis II launched on April 1st, 2026, at 06:35 PM EDT, and arrived safely back to Earth on April 10th, 2026, at 08:07:27 PM EDT.
### sc_mars_odyssey | Mars Odyssey
Still in orbit around Mars, 2001 Mars Odyssey holds the record for the longest continually active spacecraft in orbit around a planet other than Earth.
### sc_mars_reconnaissance_orbiter | Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) is a large orbiter, modeled in part on NASA’s highly successful Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft, designed to photograph Mars from orbit.
### sc_messenger | MESSENGER
MESSENGER was a NASA robotic space probe that orbited the planet Mercury between 2011 and 2015, studying Mercury's chemical composition, geology, and magnetic field.
### sc_galileo | Galileo
The <a href='https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/missions/galileo/overview/' target='_blank'>Galileo </a>mission was the first spacecraft to enter orbit around the planet Jupiter, arriving in December of 1995 and staying for eight years, and made close passes by all its major moons. Galileo even carried a small probe that it deployed and sent deep into the atmosphere of Jupiter, taking readings for almost an hour before the probe was crushed by overwhelming pressure.
### sc_magellan | Magellan
NASA's Magellan mission was the first spacecraft to image the entire surface of Venus and made several discoveries about the planet.
### sc_kepler_space_telescope | Kepler
NASA's Kepler spacecraft was launched to search for Earth-like planets orbiting other stars. It discovered more than 2,600 of these "exoplanets"—including many that are promising places for life to exist.
### sc_tess | TESS
NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite is an all-sky survey mission that will discover thousands of exoplanets around nearby bright stars.
### sc_spitzer MISSING
### sc_chandra | Chandra X-ray Observatory
Chandra allows scientists from around the world to obtain X-ray images of exotic environments to help understand the structure and evolution of the universe.
### sc_sdo | Solar Dynamics Observatory
The Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) is the first mission to be launched for NASA's Living With a Star (LWS) Program, a program designed to understand the causes of solar variability and its impacts on Earth.
### sc_ulysses | Ulysses
The Ulysses mission made nearly three complete orbits of the Sun during more than 18 years in service.
### sc_rosetta | Rosetta
<a href='https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Operations/Rosetta' target='_blank'>Rosetta </a>was a European Space Agency mission that was the first spacecraft to orbit a comet, 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko.
### sc_stardust | Stardust
NASA's <a href='https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/missions/stardust/in-depth/'target='_blank'>Stardust</a> was the first spacecraft to bring samples from a comet to Earth.
### sc_deep_impact | Deep Impact
The primary mission of NASA's <a href='https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/missions/deep-impact' target='_blank'>Deep Impact</a> was to probe beneath the surface of a comet. The spacecraft delivered a special impactor into the path of Tempel 1 to reveal never before seen materials and provide clues about the internal composition and structure of a comet. The spacecraft released its impactor which collided with the comet, and then the spacecraft observed the result.
### sc_dawn | Dawn
<a href='https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/missions/dawn/overview/' target='_blank'>Dawn</a> was the first spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies, as well as the first spacecraft to visit either Vesta or Ceres, and the first to orbit a dwarf planet.
### sc_maven | MAVEN
NASA's MAVEN studied the structure and composition of the upper atmosphere of the Red Planet.
### sc_lunar_reconnaissance_orbiter | Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) was launched in 2009 on the first U.S. mission to the Moon in over 10 years.

'true' : String(v));\n  }\n  if (time) q.set('time', time);\n  if (rate) q.set('rate', String(rate));\n  const qs = q.toString();\n  return `${NASA_APP}#/${route}${qs ? // nodes we changed, so our own edits don't loop\n\n  function entitySlug(el) {\n    const tokens = (el.className || '').split(/\\s+/).filter((t) => entityById[t]);\n    if (!tokens.length) return null;\n    return tokens.find((t) => !STRUCTURAL.has(t)) || tokens[0];\n  }\n\n  function toZh(text) {\n    const t = clean(text);\n    if (!t || hasHan(t)) return null;\n    if (uiMap[t]) return uiMap[t];\n    for (const p of patterns) {\n      const m = t.match(p.re);\n      if (m) return p.tpl.replace(/\\$(\\d+)/g, (_, i) => m[Number(i)]);\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  function setText(node, value) {\n    if (clean(node.textContent) === value) return;\n    written.add(node);\n    node.textContent = value;\n  }\n\n  function applyTo(root) {\n    if (!root || !root.querySelectorAll) return;\n\n    // 1. 3D scene labels — keyed by the entity slug the site already puts on the class.\n    for (const label of root.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div')) {\n      const slug = entitySlug(label);\n      const span = label.querySelector('.text');\n      const zh = slug && entityById[slug];\n      if (span && zh) setText(span, zh);\n    }\n\n    // 2. {
  "content": "// End-to-end test of extension/content.js against the live NASA page.\n// Headless Chrome ignores --load-extension, so this injects the exact shipped script\n// over CDP and shims only chrome.runtime.getURL, which merely resolves asset paths.\n//   node tools/test-extension.mjs [route]\nimport { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\n\nconst PORT = process.env.CDP_PORT || '9444';\nconst route = process.argv[2] || 'mars';\nconst root = new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname.replace(/^\\/(\\w:)/, '$1');\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n\nconst content = readFileSync(root + 'extension/content.js', 'utf8');\nconst names = readFileSync(root + 'data/names.zh.json', 'utf8');\nconst ui = readFileSync(root + 'data/ui.zh.json', 'utf8');\n\n// The shim mirrors what the extension does: getURL('data/x.json') -> a fetchable URL.\nconst shim = `\nwindow.__eyesZh = false;\nwindow.chrome = window.chrome || {};\nwindow.chrome.runtime = {\n  getURL: (p) => 'data:application/json;charset=utf-8,' + encodeURIComponent(\n    p.endsWith('names.zh.json') ? ${JSON.stringify(names)} : ${JSON.stringify(ui)})\n};\n`;\n\nconst list = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)).json();\nconst page = list.find((t) => t.type === 'page');\nif (!page) throw new Error('no page target on port ' + PORT);\n\nconst ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);\nawait new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));\nlet id = 0;\nconst pending = new Map();\nws.onmessage = (ev) => {\n  const m = JSON.parse(ev.data);\n  if (m.id && pending.has(m.id)) { pending.get(m.id)(m); pending.delete(m.id); }\n};\nconst send = (method, params = {}) =>\n  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const mid = ++id;\n    pending.set(mid, (m) => (m.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(m.error))) : resolve(m.result)));\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: mid, method, params }));\n  });\nconst evaluate = async (expression) => {\n  const r = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true });\n  if (r.exceptionDetails) throw new Error('page: ' + JSON.stringify(r.exceptionDetails).slice(0, 500));\n  return r.result.value;\n};\n\nawait send('Runtime.enable');\nawait send('Page.enable');\nawait send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', { width: 1600, height: 900, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false });\nawait send('Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument', { source: shim + '\\n' + content });\nawait send('Page.navigate', {\n  url: `https://eyes.nasa.gov/apps/solar-system/#/${route}`,\n});\n\n// Wait for the scene, then let the content script settle.\nfor (let i = 0; i < 150; i++) {\n  const ready = await evaluate(\n    `(async()=>{for(let i=0;i<20;i++){const ls=document.getElementById('loading-screen');\n      const done=!ls||getComputedStyle(ls).display==='none'||getComputedStyle(ls).opacity==='0';\n      if(done&&document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div').length>3)return true;\n      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,500))}return false})()`,\n  );\n  if (ready) break;\n  await sleep(1000);\n}\nawait sleep(9000);\n\nconst probe = await evaluate(`(async()=>{\n  const clean=s=>(s||'').replace(/\\\\s+/g,' ').trim();\n  const wait=ms=>new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,ms));\n  const han=/[\\\\u4e00-\\\\u9fff]/;\n  const labels=[...document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div .text')].map(e=>clean(e.textContent));\n  const rail=[...document.querySelectorAll('[aria-label]')].map(e=>clean(e.getAttribute('aria-label'))).filter(Boolean);\n  document.querySelector('button.menu-btn')?.click();\n  await wait(2500);\n  const menu=[...new Set([...document.querySelectorAll('.menu-container *')].filter(e=>!e.children.length).map(e=>clean(e.textContent)).filter(Boolean))];\n  return {\n    injected: !!window.__eyesZh,\n    title: document.title,\n    labelsZh: labels.filter(t=>han.test(t)),\n    labelsEn: labels.filter(t=>!han.test(t)),\n    railZh: rail.filter(t=>han.test(t)),\n    railEn: rail.filter(t=>!han.test(t)&&/[a-z]{3}/.test(t)),\n    menuZh: menu.filter(t=>han.test(t)).slice(0,20),\n    menuEn: menu.filter(t=>!han.test(t)).slice(0,20),\n    shareBtn: clean(document.querySelector('button.share-button')?.textContent),\n    rate: clean(document.querySelector('.rate')?.textContent),\n  };\n})()`);\n\nconst shot = await send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' });\nconst out = root + `test-extension-${route}.png`;\nconst { writeFileSync } = await import('node:fs');\nwriteFileSync(out, Buffer.from(shot.data, 'base64'));\n\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(probe, null, 2));\nconsole.log('\\nscreenshot -> ' + out);\nws.close();\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/tools/test-extension.mjs"
}

${JSON.stringify(names)} : ${JSON.stringify(ui)}) } };\nwindow.__diag = {};\n(async () => {\n  try {\n    const r = await fetch(chrome.runtime.getURL('data/ui.zh.json'));\n    const t = await r.text();\n    window.__diag.fetch = [r.ok, t.length];\n  } catch (e) { window.__diag.fetchErr = String(e); }\n  try { ${content} window.__diag.ran = true; }\n  catch (e) { window.__diag.runErr = String(e); window.__diag.stack = (e.stack || '').split('\\\\n').slice(0, 4).join(' | '); }\n})();\n'diagnostics started'`;\n\nconst list = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)).json();\nconst page = list.find((t) => t.type === 'page');\nconst ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);\nawait new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));\nlet id = 0; const pending = new Map();\nws.onmessage = (ev) => { const m = JSON.parse(ev.data); if (m.id && pending.has(m.id)) { pending.get(m.id)(m); pending.delete(m.id); } };\nconst send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((res, rej) => { const i = ++id; pending.set(i, (m) => (m.error ? rej(new Error(JSON.stringify(m.error))) : res(m.result))); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: i, method, params })); });\nconst ev = async (expression) => { const r = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true }); if (r.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.exceptionDetails).slice(0, 400)); return r.result.value; };\n\nawait send('Runtime.enable');\nconsole.log(await ev(bundle));\nawait sleep(4000);\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(await ev('window.__diag'), null, 2));\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(await ev(`(async()=>{const c=s=>(s||'').replace(/\\\\s+/g,' ').trim();const han=/[\\\\u4e00-\\\\u9fff]/;const l=[...document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div .text')].map(e=>c(e.textContent));return {zh:l.filter(t=>han.test(t)),en:l.filter(t=>!han.test(t)),title:document.title}})()`), null, 2));\nws.close();\n",

  "content": "// Dependency-free CDP driver for headless Chrome (Node >= 21, global WebSocket).\n// Usage:\n//   node cdp.mjs probe <exprFile> [url]     evaluate expression, print JSON result\n//   node cdp.mjs shot  <outPng> [url]       full screenshot\n// Chrome must already be listening: see chrome-start.mjs\nconst [mode, arg, urlArg] = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst PORT = process.env.CDP_PORT || '9333';\nconst DEFAULT_URL = 'https://eyes.nasa.gov/apps/solar-system/#/home';\n\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n\nasync function targetWs() {\n  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`);\n      const list = await res.json();\n      const page = list.find((t) => t.type === 'page');\n      if (page) return page.webSocketDebuggerUrl;\n    } catch {}\n    await sleep(500);\n  }\n  throw new Error('no CDP page target');\n}\n\nclass Cdp {\n  constructor(ws) {\n    this.ws = ws;\n    this.id = 0;\n    this.pending = new Map();\n    ws.onmessage = (ev) => {\n      const msg = JSON.parse(ev.data);\n      if (msg.id && this.pending.has(msg.id)) {\n        const { resolve, reject } = this.pending.get(msg.id);\n        this.pending.delete(msg.id);\n        msg.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result);\n      }\n    };\n  }\n  send(method, params = {}) {\n    const id = ++this.id;\n    this.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));\n    return new Promise((resolve, reject) =>\n      this.pending.set(id, { resolve, reject }),\n    );\n  }\n  async evaluate(expression) {\n    const r = await this.send('Runtime.evaluate', {\n      expression,\n      returnByValue: true,\n      awaitPromise: true,\n    });\n    if (r.exceptionDetails)\n      throw new Error('page exception: ' + JSON.stringify(r.exceptionDetails).slice(0, 800));\n    return r.result.value;\n  }\n}\n\nconst wrap = (expr) =>\n  `(async () => { const fn = (${expr}); return await fn(); })()`;\n\nasync function main() {\n  const ws = new WebSocket(await targetWs());\n  await new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));\n  ws.onerror = (e) => console.error('ws error', e.message?.value ?? '');\n  const cdp = new Cdp(ws);\n  await cdp.send('Runtime.enable');\n  await cdp.send('Page.enable');\n  await cdp.send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', {\n    width: 1600, height: 900, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false,\n  });\n\n  const url = urlArg || DEFAULT_URL;\n  await cdp.send('Page.navigate', { url });\n  // NASA Eyes streams assets for a while; poll until the scene reports ready.\n  await cdp.evaluate(\n    `(async () => {\n      for (let i = 0; i < 120; i++) {\n        const ls = document.getElementById('loading-screen');\n        const hidden = !ls || getComputedStyle(ls).display === 'none' || getComputedStyle(ls).opacity === '0';\n        if (hidden && document.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div').length > 3) return 'ready';\n        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000));\n      }\n      return 'timeout';\n    })()`,\n  );\n\n  if (mode === 'probe') {\n    const { readFileSync } = await import('node:fs');\n    const expr = readFileSync(arg, 'utf8');\n    console.log(JSON.stringify(await cdp.evaluate(wrap(expr)), null, 2));\n  } else if (mode === 'shot') {\n    const r = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' });\n    const { writeFileSync } = await import('node:fs');\n    writeFileSync(arg, Buffer.from(r.data, 'base64'));\n    console.log('wrote ' + arg);\n  } else {\n    throw new Error('unknown mode ' + mode);\n  }\n  ws.close();\n}\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error('FAIL: ' + e.message);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n",

{
  "content": "() => {\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n  const click = (sel) => { const e = document.querySelector(sel); if (e) { e.click(); return true; } return false; };\n  const notes = [];\n  // Open the right-rail panels: info, layers, settings.\n  for (const sel of ['.icon-info', '.icon-layers', '.icon-settings', '.icon-sliders', '.icon-gear', '.icon-expand']) {\n    notes.push(sel + '=' + click(sel));\n    await wait(900);\n  }\n  // Expand any collapsed section headers.\n  document.querySelectorAll('.collapsed, [class*=collapse]').forEach((e) => { try { e.click(); } catch {} });\n  await wait(1200);\n  const texts = new Set();\n  const attrs = new Set();\n  document.querySelectorAll('*').forEach((el) => {\n    if (el.children.length === 0) {\n      const t = clean(el.textContent);\n      if (t && t.length <= 120 && /[a-z]/i.test(t)) texts.add(t);\n    }\n    for (const a of ['aria-label', 'title', 'data-tippy-content', 'placeholder', 'alt']) {\n      const v = clean(el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute(a));\n      if (v && v.length <= 160) attrs.add(v);\n    }\n  });\n  return { notes, domNodes: document.querySelectorAll('*').length, texts: [...texts], attrs: [...attrs] };\n}\n",

{
  "content": "() => {\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n  const harvest = () => {\n    const texts = new Set();\n    const attrs = new Set();\n    document.querySelectorAll('*').forEach((el) => {\n      if (el.children.length === 0) {\n        const t = clean(el.textContent);\n        if (t && t.length <= 120 && /[a-z]/i.test(t)) texts.add(t);\n      }\n      for (const a of ['aria-label', 'title', 'data-tippy-content', 'placeholder', 'alt']) {\n        const v = clean(el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute(a));\n        if (v && v.length <= 160) attrs.add(v);\n      }\n    });\n    return { texts, attrs };\n  };\n  const acc = { texts: new Set(), attrs: new Set() };\n  const merge = () => { const h = harvest(); h.texts.forEach((t) => acc.texts.add(t)); h.attrs.forEach((t) => acc.attrs.add(t)); };\n  merge();\n\n  // Enumerate the right-hand settings bar icons without guessing their class names.\n  const bars = [...document.querySelectorAll('[class*=settings], [class*=shortcut], nav, aside')]\n    .filter((e) => { const r = e.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 0 && r.right > innerWidth - 140 && r.height > 40; });\n  const icons = [...new Set(bars.flatMap((b) => [...b.querySelectorAll('[class*=icon]')]))];\n  const trail = icons.map((el, i) => ({ i, cls: clean(el.className), tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase() }));\n  for (let i = 0; i < icons.length; i++) {\n    try { icons[i].click(); } catch {}\n    await wait(1100);\n    merge();\n    try { icons[i].click(); } catch {}   // close again so panels don't stack\n    await wait(500);\n  }\n  merge();\n  return {\n    route: location.hash,\n    domNodes: document.querySelectorAll('*').length,\n    iconTrail: trail,\n    texts: [...acc.texts],\n    attrs: [...acc.attrs],\n  };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/research/probe_harvest.mjs"
}
```

§1.7\n\n导出件：`research/harvest_mars.json`。\n\n### 1.7 官方 iframe 嵌入是**产品自带功能**，不是侧门\n\n站点右上角 `Share → Embed` 就是官方嵌入代码生成器。实测其输出：\n\n```html\n<iframe src=\"https://eyes.nasa.gov/apps/solar-system/#/home\" allowfullscreen ></iframe>\n```\n\n官方\"Embed Options\"面板暴露的开关（DOM 实测 input id 即 URL 参数名）：\n\n```\ninteractPrompt featured detailPanel logo search shareButton menu\ncollapseSettingsOptions hideFullScreenToggle collapseTimeControls timeControls\nlocked hideExternalLinks surfaceMapTiling hd orbiters landers majorMoons\nminorMoons heliosphere lighting flood|natural|shadow\nforceRestart maxSessionTime maxInactivityTime spout\n```\n\n`paramsToKeep`（bundle 原文）：\n`[\"time\",\"rate\",\"slide\",\"followId\",\"trajectory\",\"hideExternalLinks\",\"locked\",\"search\",\"menu\",\"timeControls\",\"hideFullScreenToggle\"]`\n\n### 1.8 URL 深层链接实测（全部通过）\n\n路由表（bundle 原文 `addRoutes([...])`）：\n\n```js\nhomeRoute            → view \"home\"\n/story/:id           → story\n/:spaceObject        → object\n/:spaceObject/compare→ compare\n/:spaceObject/telescope → telescope\n/:spaceObject/distance  → distance\n/:spaceObject/:feature  → feature\n/:spaceObject/events/:child → event\n/:spaceObject/:feature/:child → object\n```\n\n时间参数格式（bundle 原文 `_dateFormats.utc.url`）：`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ`\n\n实测结果：\n\n| 请求 URL | 实测结果 |\n|---|---|\n| `#/mars` | `document.title` → `Eyes on the Solar System - Mars - NASA/JPL`；面包屑出现 `Mars`；`mars` 标签获得 `selection` class |\n| `#/mars?time=2026-08-30T00:00:00.000Z&rate=3600` | 时钟显示 `Aug 30, 2026`，速率显示 `1 hr/s` |\n| `#/saturn?menu=false&featured=false&logo=false&shareButton=false&search=false&detailPanel=false&interactPrompt=false&hd=true&lighting=natural&rate=3600` | NASA logo / Share / Menu / 搜索 / 精选故事 / 详情面板全部消失；土星与卫星标签正常渲染 |\n\n**结论：中文站可以用 URL 参数构造\"干净画布\"，并用中文导航驱动跳转。**\n\n### 1.9 独立网站能否访问嵌入页面的内部内容（方案 B 的硬限制）\n\n在 `http://127.0.0.1:8899/embed_probe/index.html` 中放入指向 NASA Eyes 的 iframe，实测回报：\n\n```\n[load] iframe load event fired\ncontentDocument      -> null (cross-origin blocked silently)\ncontentWindow.location -> THREW: SecurityError\niframe rect = 1600x738\n```\n\n截图证据 `research/embed_probe_result.png`：火星 3D 视图、详情面板（Mars / Planet / Description / Read More / Related）、轨道器与着陆点标签、时间轴 `OCT 04, 2026 · 1 HR/S` 全部正常渲染。\n\n- ✅ 嵌入**可用**，WebGL、交互、深层链接、参数全部生效。\n- ❌ 父页面**完全无法读取或改写** iframe 内 DOM（`contentDocument` 为 `null`，访问 `location` 抛 `SecurityError`）。\n- 因此：**方案 B 对模拟器自身界面的汉化覆盖率 = 0%。** 残留英文（面包屑 `Saturn`、卫星标签 `Enceladus/Dione/Mimas/Tethys/Rhea`、`LIVE`、`OCT 14, 2026`、`1 HR/S`、右侧工具条）无法由宿主页面消除。\n\n### 1.10 许可与开源状态（不猜测）\n\n- 在 `app.js`（1.74 MB）中检索：`github.com` **0** 次、`open source`/`opensource` **0** 次、`license` **0** 次、`terms of use` **0** 次、`public domain` **0** 次。\n- 页面 `<meta name=\"robots\" content=\"noarchive\">`。\n- bundle PDF。\n\n**判定：本次调查未找到任何允许再分发 NASA Eyes 程序或素材的许可声明。因此不得声称 NASA 软件本体已开源，不得抓取或镜像其 JS/模型/纹理资源。方案 C 的\"自研 3D 层\"若依赖 NASA 资源即不可行；若完全自研则违反\"不要从零重新开发行星动力学或 3D 引擎\"的约束。**\n\n---\n\n## 二、三种汉化方案可行性比较\n\n| 维度 | A：浏览器扩展页内注入 | B：独立站 + 官方 iframe | C：独立中文交互层 |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 3D 功能保真 | 100%，不改动引擎 | 100%（官方 iframe） | 需自建引擎 → 违反约束 |\n| 天体/航天器标签汉化 | ✅ 已实测可持久改写 | ❌ 跨域不可达 | ✅ |\n| 菜单/详情/时间轴/引导汉化 | ✅ 全部 DOM，可译 | ❌ | ✅ |\n| 简介正文汉化 | ✅ 可替换 `descriptions/*.json` 渲染结果 | ❌ | 需再分发 NASA 文本 → 许可未确认 |\n| 可部署为公开网站 | ❌ 需用户手动装扩展 | ✅ GitHub Pages | ✅ |\n| 使用门槛 | 中（加载解压缩扩展） | 低（打开网址即可） | 低 |\n| NASA 改版风险 | 高：依赖 class 名与字符串 | **低**：仅依赖公开 URL 契约 | 无 |\n| 维护成本 | 中（词典 + 选择器需跟进版本） | 低（只有外壳） | 极高 |\n| 合规风险 | 低（用户本地渲染改动，不再分发资源） | 低（官方支持的嵌入） | 高（资源再分发） |\n| 覆盖不到的部分 | WebGL 内的图形文字（实测无）、NASA logo 图、`##moon_count##` 类动态模板需特殊处理 | 模拟器内**全部**英文；无法注入 CSS 之外的样式 | — |\n\n### 建议：A + B 双轨，共用一份术语数据\n\n理由（全部基于上面的实测事实）：\n\n1. 用户目标 2「界面尽可能翻译成简体中文」与目标 5「部署到 GitHub Pages」在单方案下**互斥**：只有 A 能译界面（§1.3、§1.4），只有 B 能公开托管（§1.9）。\n2. 因此把它们拆成互补交付物：**B 做中文门户 + 官方嵌入 + 中文资料层**；**A 做\"完全汉化\"增强**，由 B 站点引导安装。\n3. A 的汉化能力已被 §1.4 的实验直接证明，不是推测。\n4. C 明确否决：既无再分发许可证据（§1.10），又与\"不要自研引擎\"冲突。\n\n### 需要用户确认的技术限制（不隐瞒）\n\n- **纯静态网站无法汉化模拟器内部界面。** 若只交付 B，用户在 3D 视图里看到的仍是英文标签与英文面板。\n- 扩展 A 无法通过 GitHub Pages 一键安装，Chrome/Edge 均需\"加载解压缩的扩展\"手动步骤；Edge 还需开启\"允许来自其他商店的扩展\"以外的本地加载选项。\n- 扩展 A 依赖 NASA 页面的 class 名（`pioneer-label-div`、`<body>` 类）与英文字面量。NASA 改版会失效，需要维护。已选择**以 class 键名为主键、英文字面量为兜底**的双通道匹配来降低脆弱性。\n\n---\n\n## 三、中文界面覆盖范围（方案 A 实测可译清单）\n\n| 区域 | 具体项 | 状态 |\n|---|---|---|\n| 3D 标签 | 719 个实体 id → 中文；首批覆盖 太阳/8 行星/7 矮行星/30 主要卫星/11 彗星/重点小行星/7 着陆点/约 90 航天器 | 部分，其余保留英文并标记 |\n| 顶栏 | 标题、Share、Menu、面包屑 | 可译 |\n| 主菜单 | 分类标题、精选故事、搜索提示 | 可译 |\n| 详情面板 | Info/Toolbox/View Options、Description、More、Related、External Story、正文 | 可译 |\n| 图层/工具条 | Layers、User Interface、Planets、Trails、Orbits、Labels、Icons、光照三档、全部 `aria-label` | 可译 |\n| 时间轴 | LIVE、real rate、按钮提示、日期时间格式（**不改动数值**，仅改 `am/pm` 等词） | 可译 |\n| 新手引导 | 全部提示语与按键说明（按键字母保留原文） | 可译 |\n| 嵌入对话框 | Embed Options 全部标签与说明 | 可译 |\n| 页面标题 | `document.title` | 可译 |\n\n**无法汉化 / 不处理**：\n1. WebGL 内部的图形化文字 —— 实测该场景内不存在此类文字，故无此项损失。\n2. NASA 徽标、`EYES ON THE SOLAR SYSTEM` 品牌字样（属机构标识，按品牌规范**不应**翻译或改写）。\n3. `##moon_count##` 等运行时模板占位符 —— 需保留占位符本身，只译周围文字。\n4. 数字、日期、距离、单位 —— 按需求保持不变，不做本地化重排。\n5. 无规范译名的小天体与冷门航天器（451 颗卫星中的多数、169 个航天器中的任务代号如 `TDRS-10`、`CYGNSS 3`）—— 保留原文并标记 `untranslated`。\n\n---\n\n## 四、最小可用版本开发计划\n\n| 步 | 内容 | 验收 |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | 术语数据层：`data/names.zh.json`（id→中文+状态）、`data/ui.zh.json`（英文界面串→中文）、`data/bodies.zh.json` / `data/missions.zh.json`（译自官方 JSON，附来源 URL） | 每条含 `status` 与 `source`；无来源不写 |\n| 2 | 中文门户（纯静态、无构建）：首页、探索、天体、任务、术语对照、操作指南、关于 | 6 页可导航，标注\"非官方中文项目\" |\n| 3 | 嵌入区：按 §1.8 实测参数生成干净 iframe；中文快捷导航驱动 `#/id` 跳转；保留原始 NASA 入口 | 无头 Chrome 截图确认渲染 |\n| 4 | 扩展 A：Manifest V3 + `MutationObserver`，class 键名优先、英文字面量兜底；`pack-extension.mjs` 复用同一份词典 | §1.4 同类持久性实验通过 |\n| 5 | 本地验证：无头 Chrome 截图（门户各页 + 扩展汉化后的 NASA 页）+ Edge 兼容性检查 | 见 README 测试结果表 |\n",

  "content": "// Keeps data/names.zh.json honest: every key must exist in the entity export,\n// and the recorded English name must equal what the site actually renders\n// (verified: label text === displayName || iauName, 28/28 against the live DOM).\n//\n//   node tools/sync-glossary.mjs <entities.json> <names.zh.json> [--write]\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\n\nconst [entitiesPath, namesPath, writeFlag] = process.argv.slice(2);\nif (!entitiesPath || !namesPath) {\n  console.error('usage: node tools/sync-glossary.mjs <entities.json> <names.zh.json> [--write]');\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nconst entities = JSON.parse(readFileSync(entitiesPath, 'utf8'));\nconst byId = new Map(entities.map((e) => [e.id, e]));\nconst glossary = JSON.parse(readFileSync(namesPath, 'utf8'));\nconst label = (e) => e.displayName || e.iauName || null;\n\nconst dropped = [];\nconst fixed = [];\nconst next = {};\n\nfor (const [id, entry] of Object.entries(glossary.entities)) {\n  const real = byId.get(id);\n  if (!real || !entry.zh) {\n    dropped.push(id);\n    continue;\n  }\n  const en = label(real);\n  if (entry.en !== en) fixed.push(`${id}: \"${entry.en}\" -> \"${en}\"`);\n  next[id] = { ...entry, en, cat: real.category };\n}\n\nglossary.entities = next;\nglossary.meta.totalEntities = entities.length;\nglossary.meta.coveredEntities = Object.keys(next).length;\nglossary.meta.nameFormula = 'displayName || iauName（与站点渲染标签实测一致）';\n\nconsole.log(`covered ${Object.keys(next).length} of ${entities.length} entities`);\nif (dropped.length) console.log('dropped:\\n  ' + dropped.join('\\n  '));\nif (fixed.length) console.log('corrected:\\n  ' + fixed.join('\\n  '));\nif (writeFlag === '--write') {\n  writeFileSync(namesPath, JSON.stringify(glossary, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  console.log('written: ' + namesPath);\n}\n",

### sun | Sun
The Sun—the heart of our solar system—is a yellow dwarf star, a hot ball of glowing gases.

### mercury | Mercury
The smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun, Mercury is only slightly larger than Earth's Moon.

### venus | Venus
Similar in size and structure to Earth, Venus has been called Earth's twin. These are not identical twins, however – there are radical differences between the two worlds.

### earth | Earth
Earth—our home planet—is the only place we know of so far that’s inhabited by living things. It's also the only planet in our solar system with liquid water on the surface.

### mars | Mars
The fourth planet from the Sun, Mars is a dusty, cold, desert world with a very thin atmosphere.

### jupiter | Jupiter
Jupiter is the fifth planet from our Sun and is, by far, the largest planet in the solar system – more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

### saturn | Saturn
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second largest planet in our solar system. Adorned with thousands of beautiful ringlets, Saturn is unique among the planets. It is not the only planet to have rings—made of chunks of ice and rock—but none are as spectacular or as complicated as Saturn's. Like fellow gas giant Jupiter, Saturn is a massive ball made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

### uranus | Uranus
The seventh planet from the Sun with the third largest diameter in our solar system, Uranus is very cold and windy.

### neptune | Neptune
Dark, cold and whipped by supersonic winds, ice giant Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet in our solar system.

### 134340_pluto | Pluto
Pluto – which is smaller than Earth’s Moon – has a heart-shaped glacier that’s the size of Texas and Oklahoma. This fascinating dwarf planet has blue skies, spinning moons, mountains as high as the Rockies, and it snows – but the snow is red.

### 1_ceres | 1 Ceres
Dwarf planet Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter and the only dwarf planet located in the inner solar system.

### moon | Moon
Earth's Moon is the only place beyond Earth where humans have set foot.

### titan | Titan
Saturn’s largest moon Titan is an extraordinary and exceptional world.

### europa | Europa
Europa may be the most promising place in our solar system to find present-day environments suitable for some form of life beyond Earth.

### ganymede | Ganymede
Jupiter's moon Ganymede is the largest moon in our solar system and the only moon with its own magnetic field.

### io | Io
Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active world in the Solar System, with hundreds of volcanoes, some erupting lava fountains dozens of miles (or kilometers) high.

### callisto | Callisto
Callisto is Jupiter’s second largest moon and the third largest moon in our solar system.

### enceladus | Enceladus
One of Saturn's most surprising moons, Enceladus has altered views about where life might exist.

### triton | Triton
Triton is the largest of Neptune's [##moon_count##] moons. It is unusual because it is the only large moon in our solar system that orbits in the opposite direction of its planet's rotation―a retrograde orbit.

### charon | Charon
At half the size of Pluto, Charon is the largest of Pluto's moons and the largest known satellite relative to its parent body.

### 16_psyche | 16 Psyche
Psyche is one of the largest asteroids in the solar system, and is mostly made of metal.

### 101955_bennu | 101955 Bennu
An ancient relic of our solar system’s early days, Bennu has seen more than 4.5 billion years of history. Scientists think that within 10 million years of our solar system’s formation, Bennu’s present-day composition was already established.

### sc_voyager_1 | Voyager 1
No spacecraft has gone farther than NASA's Voyager 1. Launched in 1977 to fly by Jupiter and Saturn, Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to collect data.
### sc_voyager_2 | Voyager 2
NASA's Voyager 2 is the second spacecraft to enter interstellar space. On Dec. 10, 2018, the spacecraft joined its twin—Voyager 1—as the only human-made objects to enter the space between the stars.
### sc_pioneer_10 | Pioneer 10
Launched in 1972, Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to visit Jupiter. Its mission ended in 2003, but it is one of four spacecraft (including the two Voyagers and Pioneer 11) carrying a message from Earth beyond our solar system.
### sc_pioneer_11 | Pioneer 11
Launched in 1973, Pioneer 11 was the first spacecraft to fly past Saturn. Its mission ended in 1995, but it is one of four spacecraft (including the two Voyagers and Pioneer 10) carrying a message from Earth beyond our solar system.
### sc_new_horizons | New Horizons
New Horizons is a NASA mission to study the dwarf planet Pluto, its moons, and other objects in the Kuiper Belt, a region of the solar system that extends from about 30 AU, near the orbit of Neptune, to about 50 AU from the Sun.
### sc_cassini | Cassini
For more than a decade, NASA’s Cassini spacecraft shared the wonders of Saturn and its family of icy moons—taking us to astounding worlds where methane rivers run to a methane sea and where jets of ice and gas are blasting material into space from a liquid water ocean that might harbor the ingredients for life. Cassini revealed in great detail the true wonders of Saturn, a giant world ruled by raging storms and delicate harmonies of gravity.
### sc_juno | Juno
Juno is studying the interior and origins of giant planet Jupiter for the first time. It has been orbiting Jupiter since it arrived in 2016.
### sc_europa_clipper | Europa Clipper
Europa Clipper will search for signs of potential habitability on Jupiter's icy ocean moon Europa.
### sc_parker_solar_probe | Parker Solar Probe
NASA's Parker Solar Probe is on a mission to "touch the Sun." The spacecraft is flying closer to the Sun’s surface than any spacecraft before it. The mission will revolutionize our understanding of the Sun.
### sc_jwst | James Webb Space Telescope
The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is a large infrared telescope with an approximately 6.5 meter primary mirror.
### sc_hubble_space_telescope | Hubble Space Telescope
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope is the first astronomical observatory placed into orbit around Earth with the ability to record images in wavelengths of light spanning from ultraviolet to near-infrared.
### sc_roman_space_telescope | Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
Named after NASA’s first chief astronomer, the ‘mother of the Hubble Space Telescope,’ the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble's, potentially measuring light from a billion galaxies in its lifetime. The mission launched on August 30, 2026.
### sc_mars_2020 | Perseverance
The Perseverance rover is looking for signs of ancient life and is collecting rock and soil samples for a possible return to Earth by a subsequent Mars mission.
### sc_mars_science_laboratory | Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity)
Part of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory mission, Curiosity was the largest and most capable rover ever sent to Mars at the time of launch.
### sc_insight | InSight
NASA's InSight lander (Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport) is the first mission to study the deep interior of Mars.
### sc_phoenix | Phoenix
NASA's Phoenix mission landed farther north on Mars than any previous spacecraft to date. The lander verified the presence of water-ice on Mars by actually scooping it up and analyzing it.
### sc_iss | International Space Station (ISS)
The International Space Station (ISS) is a permanently crewed on-orbit laboratory that enables scientific research supporting innovation on Earth and future deep space exploration.
### sc_lucy | Lucy
The <a href='https://science.nasa.gov/mission/lucy/' target='_blank'>Lucy</a> spacecraft will explore a record-breaking number of asteroids, flying by two asteroids in the solar system’s main asteroid belt, and by eight Trojan asteroids that share an orbit around the Sun with Jupiter.
### sc_psyche | Psyche
The <a href='https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/missions/psyche' target='_blank'>Psyche</a> mission launched on October 13th, 2023, and will explore the origin of planetary cores by studying the metallic asteroid of the same name.
### sc_osiris_rex | OSIRIS-APEX (OSIRIS-REx)
NASA’s <a href='https://www.nasa.gov/osiris-rex' target='_blank'>OSIRIS-REx</a> was the first U.S. mission to deliver an asteroid sample to Earth on September 24th, 2023. The spacecraft, renamed OSIRIS-APEX after the delivery, is now headed to asteroid Apophis for a 2029 rendezvous.
### sc_dart | DART
<a href='https://dart.jhuapl.edu/' target='_blank'>DART</a>, or Double Asteroid Redirection Test, was the first attempt to change the course of an asteroid with a kinetic impact.
### sc_artemis_1 | Artemis I
Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test that was the first mission to use NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and the Orion spacecraft. It was followed by a crewed flight on Artemis II in April of 2026.
### sc_artemis_2 | Artemis II
Artemis II built on the success of the uncrewed Artemis I in 2022, and demonstrated a broad range of capabilities needed on deep space missions. The Artemis II test flight was NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft. The Artemis II crew traveled approximately 6,545 kilometers (4,067 miles) beyond the far side of the Moon on April 6th, 2026, setting a human spaceflight distance record. Artemis II launched on April 1st, 2026, at 06:35 PM EDT, and arrived safely back to Earth on April 10th, 2026, at 08:07:27 PM EDT.
### sc_mars_odyssey | Mars Odyssey
Still in orbit around Mars, 2001 Mars Odyssey holds the record for the longest continually active spacecraft in orbit around a planet other than Earth.
### sc_mars_reconnaissance_orbiter | Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) is a large orbiter, modeled in part on NASA’s highly successful Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft, designed to photograph Mars from orbit.
### sc_messenger | MESSENGER
MESSENGER was a NASA robotic space probe that orbited the planet Mercury between 2011 and 2015, studying Mercury's chemical composition, geology, and magnetic field.
### sc_galileo | Galileo
The <a href='https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/missions/galileo/overview/' target='_blank'>Galileo </a>mission was the first spacecraft to enter orbit around the planet Jupiter, arriving in December of 1995 and staying for eight years, and made close passes by all its major moons. Galileo even carried a small probe that it deployed and sent deep into the atmosphere of Jupiter, taking readings for almost an hour before the probe was crushed by overwhelming pressure.
### sc_magellan | Magellan
NASA's Magellan mission was the first spacecraft to image the entire surface of Venus and made several discoveries about the planet.
### sc_kepler_space_telescope | Kepler
NASA's Kepler spacecraft was launched to search for Earth-like planets orbiting other stars. It discovered more than 2,600 of these "exoplanets"—including many that are promising places for life to exist.
### sc_tess | TESS
NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite is an all-sky survey mission that will discover thousands of exoplanets around nearby bright stars.
### sc_spitzer MISSING
### sc_chandra | Chandra X-ray Observatory
Chandra allows scientists from around the world to obtain X-ray images of exotic environments to help understand the structure and evolution of the universe.
### sc_sdo | Solar Dynamics Observatory
The Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) is the first mission to be launched for NASA's Living With a Star (LWS) Program, a program designed to understand the causes of solar variability and its impacts on Earth.
### sc_ulysses | Ulysses
The Ulysses mission made nearly three complete orbits of the Sun during more than 18 years in service.
### sc_rosetta | Rosetta
<a href='https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Operations/Rosetta' target='_blank'>Rosetta </a>was a European Space Agency mission that was the first spacecraft to orbit a comet, 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko.
### sc_stardust | Stardust
NASA's <a href='https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/missions/stardust/in-depth/'target='_blank'>Stardust</a> was the first spacecraft to bring samples from a comet to Earth.
### sc_deep_impact | Deep Impact
The primary mission of NASA's <a href='https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/missions/deep-impact' target='_blank'>Deep Impact</a> was to probe beneath the surface of a comet. The spacecraft delivered a special impactor into the path of Tempel 1 to reveal never before seen materials and provide clues about the internal composition and structure of a comet. The spacecraft released its impactor which collided with the comet, and then the spacecraft observed the result.
### sc_dawn | Dawn
<a href='https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/missions/dawn/overview/' target='_blank'>Dawn</a> was the first spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies, as well as the first spacecraft to visit either Vesta or Ceres, and the first to orbit a dwarf planet.
### sc_maven | MAVEN
NASA's MAVEN studied the structure and composition of the upper atmosphere of the Red Planet.
### sc_lunar_reconnaissance_orbiter | Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) was launched in 2009 on the first U.S. mission to the Moon in over 10 years.

'true' : String(v));\n  }\n  if (time) q.set('time', time);\n  if (rate) q.set('rate', String(rate));\n  const qs = q.toString();\n  return `${NASA_APP}#/${route}${qs ? Verified by\n// measurement on 2026-10-11 (docs/技术调查报告.md §1.3–1.4).\n//\n// We never touch the WebGL canvas, the simulation, or any numeric value.\n(() => {\n  'use strict';\n  if (window.__eyesZh) return;\n  window.__eyesZh = true;\n\n  // Class tokens that describe a category or a UI state rather than an entity.\n  // Needed because a label for Ganymede carries the tokens \"ganymede moon\",\n  // and \"moon\" is itself an entity id (Earth's Moon).\n  const STRUCTURAL = new Set([\n    'no-select', 'clickable', 'hidden', 'hiddenByLabelQuadtree', 'selection', 'selected',\n    'star', 'planet', 'moon', 'dwarf', 'asteroid', 'comet', 'spacecraft', 'galaxy',\n    'universe', 'landing', 'site', 'instrument', 'vehicle', 'human', 'building',\n    'orbiter', 'lander', 'rover', 'major', 'minor',\n  ]);\n\n  const ATTRS = ['aria-label', 'title', 'data-tippy-content', 'placeholder'];\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  const hasHan = (s) => /[一-鿿]/.test(s);\n\n  let entityById = {};\n  let uiMap = {};\n  let patterns = [];\n  const written = new WeakSet(); // nodes we changed, so our own edits don't loop\n\n  function entitySlug(el) {\n    const tokens = (el.className || '').split(/\\s+/).filter((t) => entityById[t]);\n    if (!tokens.length) return null;\n    return tokens.find((t) => !STRUCTURAL.has(t)) || tokens[0];\n  }\n\n  function toZh(text) {\n    const t = clean(text);\n    if (!t || hasHan(t)) return null;\n    if (uiMap[t]) return uiMap[t];\n    for (const p of patterns) {\n      const m = t.match(p.re);\n      if (m) return p.tpl.replace(/\\$(\\d+)/g, (_, i) => m[Number(i)]);\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  function setText(node, value) {\n    if (clean(node.textContent) === value) return;\n    written.add(node);\n    node.textContent = value;\n  }\n\n  function applyTo(root) {\n    if (!root || !root.querySelectorAll) return;\n\n    // 1. 3D scene labels — keyed by the entity slug the site already puts on the class.\n    for (const label of root.querySelectorAll('.pioneer-label-div')) {\n      const slug = entitySlug(label);\n      const span = label.querySelector('.text');\n      const zh = slug && entityById[slug];\n      if (span && zh) setText(span, zh);\n    }\n\n    // 2. [root] : [...root.querySelectorAll('*')];\n    for (const el of leaves) {\n      if (el.classList?.contains('pioneer-label-div')) continue;\n      if (!el.children.length && el.textContent && !el.closest('.pioneer-label-div')) {\n        const zh = toZh(el.textContent);\n        if (zh) setText(el, zh);\n      }\n      for (const attr of ATTRS) {\n        const v = el.getAttribute?.(attr);\n        const zh = v && toZh(v);\n        if (zh) { written.add(el); el.setAttribute(attr, zh); }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  function translateTitle() {\n    const page = location.hash.replace(/^#\\/?/, '').split('?')[0].split('/')[0] || 'home';\n    const name = entityById[page];\n    const wanted = name ? `太阳系探索 - ${name} - NASA/JPL（非官方中文）` : null;\n    if (wanted && document.title !== wanted) {\n      written.add(document);\n      document.title = wanted;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // ---- batching: one pass per frame, and our own writes never re-enter ----\n  const queued = new Set();\n  let frame = 0;\n  function flush() {\n    frame = 0;\n    for (const node of queued) if (node.isConnected) applyTo(node);\n    queued.clear();\n    translateTitle();\n  }\n  function schedule(node) {\n    queued.add(node?.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE ? node : document.body);\n    if (!frame) frame = requestAnimationFrame(flush);\n  }\n\n  new MutationObserver((records) => {\n    for (const r of records) {\n      const touched = r.type === 'characterData'\n        ? - 18 张验证截图在 `shots/`

## 没做的两项

1. **Edge 桌面端实测** — 本轮所有验证只在 Chrome 155 上跑。
2. **扩展的真实加载确认** — `headless=new` 会忽略 `--load-extension`，所以我是用 CDP 注入同一份 `content.js`（只给 `chrome.runtime.getURL` 打桩）验证的。翻译逻辑已证明有效，但 manifest 是否被真实浏览器接受、`document_idle` 注入是否正常，需要你手动"加载已解压的扩展"跑一次。

这两项我已建成任务 #9、#10 挂在清单上。

另外那个**必须让你知道的技术限制**仍然成立：纯静态站对嵌入的模拟器界面汉化率是 0%（实测 `contentDocument` 为 `null`、访问 `location` 抛 `SecurityError`）。所以"界面尽可能翻译成中文"这个目标只能靠扩展达成，静态站做不到，我也没有去绕同源策略。

Umbriel is the darkest of Uranus' largest moons. It reflects only 16 percent of the light that strikes its surface, a feature similar to the highland areas of Earth's Moon.

Halley's Comet or Comet Halley, officially designated 1P/Halley, is a short-period comet visible from Earth every 75–76 years. Halley is the only known short-period comet that is regularly visible to the naked eye from Earth, and the only naked-eye comet that can appear twice in a human lifetime.

### sc_soho | SOHO | label=SOHO | cat=Spacecraft
SOHO is the longest-lived Sun-watching satellite to date. Numerous mission extensions have enabled the spacecraft to observe two 11-year solar cycles and to discover thousands of comets.

### sc_clementine | Clementine | label=Clementine | cat=Spacecraft
Clementine was the first U.S. spacecraft launched to the Moon in over 20 years. It was designed to test spacecraft components during extended exposure to space and to study the Moon and an asteroid.

### sc_grail_a | GRAIL A | label=GRAIL A | cat=Spacecraft
NASA's GRAIL mission flew twin spacecraft—Ebb and Flow—in tandem around the Moon to map variations in the lunar gravitational field

### sc_mars_express | Mars Express | label=Mars Express | cat=Spacecraft
The Mars Express mission is exploring the planet Mars, and is the first planetary mission attempted by the European Space Agency (ESA).

### sc_trace_gas_orbiter | Trace Gas Orbiter | label=Trace Gas Orbiter | cat=Spacecraft
The ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (ExoMars TGO) is searching for methane and other trace gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence of possible biological or geological activity. The orbiter is the first in a series of joint missions between the European Space Agency (ESA) and Roscosmos, the Russian space agency.

### sc_mariner_2 | Mariner 2 | label=Mariner 2 | cat=Spacecraft
NASA's Mariner 2 was the world's first successful interplanetary spacecraft. The spacecraft flew by Venus, sending back valuable new information about interplanetary space and the Venusian atmosphere.

### sc_huygens | Huygens | label=Huygens | cat=Spacecraft
The European Space Agency's Huygens Probe was a unique, advanced spacecraft and a crucial part of the overall Cassini mission to explore Saturn.

- makemake 鸟神星: "鸟神星与冥王星、阋神星、妊神星这几颗矮行星一样，位于海王星轨道之外的柯伊伯带区域。"
- sedna 塞德娜: "塞德娜是一颗可能属于矮行星的天体，位于海王星轨道之外很远的地方。它的轨道极为细长，绕太阳一周约需 11,400 年。"
- phobos 火卫一: "火卫一是火星两颗卫星中较大的一颗。它每天绕火星运行三圈，且离火星表面极近，以致在火星上的某些位置并不能始终看到它。"
- deimos 火卫二: "火卫二是火星两颗卫星中较小的一颗。它的尺寸仅约 9 × 7 × 6.8 英里（15 × 12 × 11 公里），每 30 小时环绕火星一周。"
- iapetus 土卫八: "土卫八是土星第三大的卫星，以一半明亮、一半黑暗著称，其前导半球是暗色的。"
- rhea 土卫五: "土卫五是土星第二大的卫星。"
- dione 土卫四: "土卫四是一颗较小的卫星，每 2.7 天环绕土星一周，其轨道距离与月球绕地球的距离大致相当。"
- tethys 土卫三: "土卫三是土星第五大的卫星。"
- mimas 土卫一: "布满撞击坑的土卫一是土星主要卫星中最小、也是最靠近土星的一颗。"

- titania 天卫三: "天卫三是天王星最大的卫星。旅行者 2 号在天卫三被发现近 200 年后拍摄的图像显示，这颗卫星曾有过地质活动。"
- oberon 天卫四: "天卫四是天王星第二大的卫星。"
- ariel 天卫一: "天卫一是天王星的一颗卫星。"
- umbriel 天卫二: "天卫二在天王星的大型卫星中最为黑暗。它只反射照射到其表面光线的 16%，这一特征与月球的高地区域相似。"
- 4_vesta 灶神星: "灶神星是小行星带中最大的天体之一，NASA 的黎明号航天器曾对其进行长达一年多的探测。"
- 2_pallas 智神星: "智神星是继谷神星之后第二颗被发现的小行星。"
- 162173_ryugu 龙宫小行星: "龙宫是一颗轨道可能非常接近地球的小行星。隼鸟2号任务于 2018 年造访它，采集了其表面样本，并于 2020 年 12 月将小行星物质送回地球。"
- 486958_arrokoth 阿罗科思: "这颗小型柯伊伯带天体的正式名称为阿罗科思（Arrokoth），是航天器迄今探测过的距离最远、也最原始的天体。"

- dimorphos 迪莫弗斯: "迪莫弗斯是一颗与较大小行星迪迪莫斯组成双星系统的小行星，轨道周期为 11.9 小时。"
- 1p_halley 哈雷彗星: "哈雷彗星（Halley's Comet），正式编号 1P/Halley，是一颗短周期彗星，每 75–76 年可从地球观测到一次。哈雷彗星是已知唯一一颗能定期以肉眼从地球看到的短周期彗星，也是唯一一颗能在人一生中出现的肉眼可见彗星。"
- 67p 丘留莫夫－格拉西缅科彗星: "67P/丘留莫夫－格拉西缅科彗星创造了历史——它是第一颗被来自地球的航天器环绕并着陆的彗星。"

{
  "command": "cd \"C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6\" && node -e \"\nconst fs=require('fs');\nconst ids=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('research/sc_ids.json','utf8'));\nconst src = \\`\n() => {\n  const ids = \\${JSON.stringify(ids)};\n  const titles = {};\n  const errs = {};\n  let ok = 0;\n  // 12 at a time so we do not hammer the CDN.\n  for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i += 12) {\n    const batch = ids.slice(i, i + 12);\n    await Promise.all(batch.map(async (id) => {\n      try {\n        const r = await fetch('/apps/solar-system/events/' + id + '/all_events.json');\n        if (!r.ok) { errs[r.status] = (errs[r.status] || 0) + 1; return; }\n        const j = await r.json();\n        ok++;\n        for (const e of Object.values(j)) {\n          if (e && e.title) (titles[e.title] ||= []).push(id);\n        }\n      } catch (err) { errs.fetch = (errs.fetch || 0) + 1; }\n    }));\n  }\n  return JSON.stringify({ filesOk: ok, errs, distinctTitles: Object.keys(titles).length, titles: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(titles).map(([k, v]) => [k, v.length])) });\n}\\`;\nfs.writeFileSync('research/probe_fetch_events.mjs', src + '\\n');\nconsole.log('probe written,', ids.length, 'ids');\n\"",
  "description": "Generate batch event-fetch probe"
}

Title: 土星卫星
Link: https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9C%9F%E6%98%9F%E5%8D%AB%E6%98%9F/4338243
Snippet: 土星卫星已确认的最少有10颗。按与土星距离由近及远排列为： 土卫十 、 土卫一 、 土卫二 、 土卫三 、 土卫四 、 土卫五 、 土卫六 、 土卫七 、 土卫八 、 土卫九 。据报道1979年9月1日行星际探测器“先驱者”11号又发现一颗新卫星，暂取名“先驱岩”（Pioneerrock）或1979S1，但尚未确认。其中土卫十离土星的距离只有159,500公里，仅为 土星赤道 半径的2.66倍，已接近 洛希极限 。土卫八的轨道面与土星赤道面的交角为14°7，而其轨道面与土星的公转轨道面的交角为16°3，是 不规则卫星 ；土卫九在一个 偏心率 达0.1633的 椭圆轨道 上绕土星公转，其轨道面与土星赤道面的交角约为150°，也是不规则卫星。除土卫八和土卫九外，土卫一至土卫七以及 土卫十 都是规则卫星，在土星赤道平面附近以近圆轨道绕土星转动。在土卫一至土卫十这10颗土星卫星中，土卫九是唯一的逆行卫星，因为它的轨道面与土星的公转轨道面的交角为174°42┡，它绕土星的转动方向和土星绕太阳的转动方向相反。
PublishedTime: 2025-06-03T00:00:00+08:00

Title: 土星的卫星- 维基百科，自由的百科全书
Link: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-cn/%E5%9C%9F%E6%98%9F%E7%9A%84%E8%A1%9B%E6%98%9F?useFormat=mobile
Snippet: [18]1966年，奥杜安·多尔菲斯趁土星位于分点，即土星环平行于视线时，进行观测，发现了土卫十。[19]若干年后，科学家发现，要完全解释1966年的观测数据，一定还存在着另一颗轨道与土卫十相似的卫星，这就是土卫十一。
[20]
航天器观测
[编辑]自从使用了无人空间探测器，人们对外行星的研究发生了根本性的变化。旅行者计划航天器抵达土星后，在1980至81年间发现了三颗卫星：土卫十五、土卫十六和土卫十七。[20]此外，旅行者号还证实了土卫十和土卫十一是两颗不同的卫星。
科学家相信，土卫九原是柯伊伯带的一颗半人马小行星，后被土星的引力捕获。[29]土卫九还是土星最大环物质的来源，也是土卫八有漆黑一面的原因。[77]

Snippet: 土卫十二是土卫四的特洛伊卫星，土卫十三和土卫十四则是土卫三的特洛伊卫星。
太空船观测
自从使用了无人太空探测器，人们对外行星的研究发生了根本性的变化。旅行者计划太空船抵达土星后，在1980至81年间发现了三颗卫星：土卫十五、土卫十六和土卫十七。此外，旅行者号还证实了土卫十和土卫十一是两颗不同的卫星。
、土卫五十一、土卫五十四、土卫五十五、土卫五十六、土卫五十七、土卫五十九、土卫六十一、土卫六十二、土卫六十三、土卫六十五、土卫六十六以及15颗未命名卫星。
科学家相信，土卫九原是凯伯带的一颗半人马小行星，后被土星的引力捕获。土卫九还是土星最大环物质的来源，也是土卫八有漆黑一面的原因。

Snippet: [43]
土卫十和土卫十一是太阳系中唯一一对共轨卫星。[20]它们体积相近，土卫十比土卫十一稍大。[43]两者轨道半长轴只有几公里之差，如果相互掠过的话，就会相撞。不过事实上，引力作用使得两者的轨道每四年交换一次。
它们离土星的距离（192至307个土星半径）、轨道倾角（44°至50°）、颜色都十分相近，故归为一群。[30][39]
高卢卫星群由四颗位于外圈的顺行卫星所组成：土卫二十一、土卫二十六、土卫二十八及土卫三十七，其中土卫二十六最大，直径约为32公里。
土星环及三颗卫星：土卫一、土卫二及土卫三
诺尔斯卫星群（又称土卫九卫星群）由46颗位于外圈的逆行卫星所组成：土卫九、土卫十九、土卫二十三、土卫二十五、土卫二十七、土卫三十、土卫三十一、土卫三十六、土卫三十八、土卫三十九、土卫四十、土卫四十一、土卫四十二、土卫四十三、土卫四十四、土卫四十五、土卫四十六、

{
  "content": "() => {\n  const clean = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();\n  // The satellite tables on the Chinese Wikipedia planet articles carry a\n  // \"编号\" column of Chinese numerals next to the Latin name. Pair them.\n  const pairs = [];\n  for (const tr of document.querySelectorAll('table tr')) {\n    const cells = [...tr.querySelectorAll('th,td')].map((c) => clean(c.innerText));\n    const idx = cells.findIndex((c) => /^[一二三四五六七八九十百零]+$/.test(c));\n    if (idx === -1 || idx > 2) continue;\n    const numeral = cells[idx];\n    const latin = cells.slice(idx + 1).find((c) => /^[†♠‡♦♣\\s]*[A-Z][A-Za-z'’\\- ]{2,24}$/.test(c));\n    if (!latin) continue;\n    pairs.push({ numeral, latin: latin.replace(/[†♠♦♣]/g, '').trim() });\n  }\n  const seen = new Set();\n  const uniq = pairs.filter((p) => { const k = p.latin + '|' + p.numeral; if (seen.has(k)) return false; seen.add(k); return true; });\n  return { title: document.title, count: uniq.length, pairs: uniq };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "C:/Users/lenovo/Documents/Qoder/2026-10-11/4555adb6/research/probe_wiki_moons.mjs"
}
```
